answer: The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, slashed on a failed audit, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. A vine of per-task receipts records who did what, and the zenith of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the inlet of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
